selects.note: The console commit this publication SELECTS, as distinct from `commit` above, which is the landing repo commit that was published. Promoted from prose to a field so currency is a one-hop derivation: resolved CID -> this record -> selects.commit, compared against the artifact's own CONSOLE_SOURCE_COMMIT. Without it the honest verdict is COULD_NOT_CHECK/lock_unreadable — a structural inability to establish currency, never STALE, and never licence to infer it through another repo's history.

purpose: Republishes the console from cross-reference-console@f3e9a67 — console.lock had been at 2436082 since 2026-08-10, fifteen commits behind. Among them was the lineage-marker extraction (crc 0cafaaa): before it, an edge whose lineage state could not be determined rendered as a plain green with no qualifier at all, because the marker was guarded by `if (lin)` and linClaimState returns null below two lanes. Absence of a state was rendered as absence of a caveat, which reads as the strongest claim on the page. The published console carried that for five days after the fix merged. Also carries the currency section of PIN-RECORD.md and check_boardy_rule.py, which asserts the state-to-text mapping the console ships rather than a copy of it.
how_it_went_unnoticed: Three checks were green throughout and each was honest about its own link: build/sync_console.py --check (console/index.html IS the build of the commit in console.lock), cross-reference-console's check_console_reproducible.py (ui/index.html IS the deterministic build of its commit), and check_console_currency.py (the contenthash IS the site-tree of landing HEAD). None was wrong. The LOCK was, and nothing was looking at the lock. A pin is a claim about which commit is published; it is never a claim that it is the one you would want. build/check_console_currency.py in the landing repo now reports CURRENT / STALE / UNDETERMINED on the lock itself.

verification.note: Read from the resolver contract directly and decoded from the raw e30101701220 bytes, not from a resolver API. Two independent ENS APIs served the superseded CID for some minutes after the transaction confirmed at block 25760403; the contract did not. A cached read is not a second opinion.

availability.note: build/site_cid.py DERIVES the CID with `ipfs add -n`, which stores nothing. The bytes were added separately with identical cid_params and reproduced this exact CID, then pinned locally and on Pinata by hash rather than re-uploaded — re-uploading risks a different CID under the pinning service's own defaults, which would silently break this record.
